claim: During the 15-day Eid-ul-Fitr 2026 travel period, 351 people were killed, averaging 23 deaths per day.
notes: Average is 351 divided by 15 = 23.4 per day; the live report rounds to 23 per day. The headline period is outside the cleaned dataset's 2022-2024 range.
sources: Road Safety Foundation and Bangladesh Jatri Kalyan Samity, Eid-ul-Fitr 2026 travel monitoring, as published in the live report; underlying reports not yet archived in the bureau's evidence repository

claim: The WHO-modelled road death estimate, about 31,578 per year, is 5.8 times the BRTA official count of 5,480.
notes: Ratio is 31,578 divided by 5,480 = 5.76, rounded to 5.8. Definitions differ: BRTA counts police-FIR deaths, WHO uses a modelled 30-day definition.
sources: WHO modelled estimate 2023, as published in the live report
BRTA official count 2023, as published in the live report

claim: The joma daily-lease system forces bus drivers to race for passengers, because drivers pay a fixed daily fee before earning.
notes: Figures are attributed to TIB, not independently replicated by the bureau. Daily fee reported as BDT 4,000 to 6,000, rising to Tk 8,000 or more during Eid; net driver income reported as BDT 300 to 500 per day.
sources: Transparency International Bangladesh 2024 transport survey, as cited in the live report

claim: Banned fleets re-emerge under new operator names on the same routes — the Phoenix pattern. Route continuity is probable; ownership continuity is alleged, not confirmed by a corporate registry.
notes: No operator is found guilty unless a specific conviction is cited. No beneficial ownership is asserted.
sources: Live report, Phoenix scene: High Court and BRTA ban on Suprobhat Paribahan, Sadarghat-Gazipur corridor, 2019 crash context; family and victim testimony for ownership continuity

claim: Four datasets the government holds are not published: BRTA bus crash registry by chassis, hospital trauma records linked to crash cause, police FIRs linked to operator name, and a route-permit beneficial-owner registry.
notes: This is a confirmed absence finding: each dataset is held or should exist and is not published in the form needed.
sources: Live report, Voids scene VOID-01 to VOID-04

claim: The deduplicated dataset (47,680 raw rows reduced to 2,331 unique accidents, because 95.11% of raw rows were artificial padding created by cross-joining single accidents across permuted metadata values) shows heavy clustering at highway entry and exit corridors and roundabouts.
notes: Live report scene heading says 2,332; this report uses 2,331, the audited count, and flags the one-record difference.
sources: Figshare dataset 'Bangladesh Road Traffic Accident Dataset (2007-2024): Multi-Source Integration', DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.30631292.v1; bureau deduplication audit as published in the live report

claim: 41.56% of fatal Dhaka crashes occur between 10pm and 6am, and pedestrians account for 47% of Dhaka road victims (Road Safety Foundation).
notes: The earlier 97.13 percent night-time figure was corrected to 41.56 percent; see Corrections on the page.
sources: Road Safety Foundation, Dhaka Annual Report 2025 basis, as corrected 2026-06-08 (correction C-001)
